comment: Spec 058 section 13.1. Every diagnostic the fabric CLI (FC-), the SDKs (FW-), the host emitter (FE-), the reader (FR-) and the Node (FN-) emit, with a stable id, a fixed text, a fix and a docs anchor. Texts and fixes carry no interpolated value: a host name, path or variable value appears only in local output (status files, CLI output), never on telemetry. Each id's docs anchor is its lowercase id in the docs page. Ids are never reused; a retired id stays listed with retired: true.

messages.name: capture_not_installed
messages.text: wire capture is not installed: the configuration is invalid
messages.fix: run `python -m fabric.wire status` with the agent's environment; it names the setting and the fix

messages.name: no_destination
messages.text: spans have no destination: no OTLP endpoint is set, so captured spans are dropped
messages.fix: set FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) to the Fabric Node, for example http://127.0.0.1:4318 for a local Node

messages.name: no_store
messages.text: no content store is configured: capture is metadata only, request and response bodies are not kept
messages.fix: set FABRIC_WIRE_STORE=node with FABRIC_WIRE_CONTENT_ENDPOINT, or FABRIC_WIRE_STORE=file:///absolute/dir for a local trial

messages.name: redacted_roles
messages.text: the capture policy masks some content roles and the autoload has no transformation for them: their content is withheld
messages.fix: give those roles retain_original or metadata_only in the capture policy, or install in code with transformations= and FABRIC_REDACTION_ENDPOINT

messages.name: endpoint_set
messages.text: the model endpoints recorded by this process
messages.fix: add a host with FABRIC_WIRE_ENDPOINTS, or pin the built-in rows of an earlier release with FABRIC_WIRE_BUILTIN_ENDPOINTS=legacy

messages.name: unmatched_model_host
messages.text: a model-looking request matched no configured endpoint and was not recorded
messages.fix: add the host to FABRIC_WIRE_ENDPOINTS; the status lists the exact value for each host

messages.name: otel_sdk_disabled
messages.text: capture is disabled by OTEL_SDK_DISABLED: nothing is recorded
messages.fix: unset OTEL_SDK_DISABLED in the agent's environment

messages.name: content_capture_disabled
messages.text: content capture is disabled for this profile; metadata capture continues
messages.fix: the status names the reason; give the production profile a capture policy, an id key and a spool key, or use the local profile

messages.name: spool_backlog
messages.text: records wait in the spool and no process is draining it
messages.fix: run `python -m fabric.wire drain --until-empty` with the agent's environment; for batch or serverless workers set FABRIC_WIRE_DRAIN_ON_EXIT_S

messages.name: otlp_url_credentials
messages.text: an endpoint URL carries credentials, a query or a fragment
messages.fix: remove user:password@, ?query and #fragment from the URL; send credentials as headers (FABRIC_OTLP_HEADERS_FILE or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS)

messages.name: otlp_exporter_missing
messages.text: the OTLP exporter package is not installed
messages.fix: pip install "singleaxis-fabric[otlp]" in the agent's environment

messages.name: otlp_plaintext_non_loopback
messages.text: the OTLP endpoint uses http to a non-loopback host
messages.fix: use https with FABRIC_OTLP_CERTIFICATE (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE), or a loopback address (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1])

messages.name: otlp_endpoint_missing
messages.text: this delivery mode needs an OTLP traces endpoint
messages.fix: set FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT) to the Fabric Node, for example http://127.0.0.1:4318 for a local Node

messages.name: endpoints_invalid_json
messages.text: FABRIC_WIRE_ENDPOINTS is not a JSON array of matcher objects
messages.fix: use a JSON array such as [{"endpoint_id":"my-model","dialect":"openai","hosts":["models.example.com"]}]

messages.name: endpoint_matcher_invalid
messages.text: an endpoint matcher is invalid
messages.fix: each entry needs an endpoint_id and provider_name of lowercase letters, digits and ._-, dialect openai or anthropic, hosts or host_suffixes, schemes http/https and ports 1-65535

messages.name: protected_global_provider
messages.text: a Fabric-protected global tracer provider cannot carry wire spans
messages.fix: set FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT (or OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT): capture then delivers through its own private tracer provider

messages.name: fabric_otlp_without_endpoint
messages.text: a FABRIC_OTLP_* setting is set without FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT
messages.fix: set FABRIC_OTLP_ENDPOINT, or remove the other FABRIC_OTLP_* variables

messages.name: key_value_and_file
messages.text: a key is set both as a value and as a file
messages.fix: set either the variable or its _FILE variant, not both

messages.name: secret_file_unreadable
messages.text: a key, certificate or headers file is missing, unreadable or malformed
messages.fix: check the path and the permissions of the file the reason names

messages.name: builtin_endpoints_invalid
messages.text: FABRIC_WIRE_BUILTIN_ENDPOINTS has an unknown value
messages.fix: use table (the default: every qualified built-in row) or legacy (the three rows of releases before 0.13)

messages.name: llm_content_ignored
messages.text: FABRIC_CAPTURE_LLM_CONTENT does not affect wire capture
messages.fix: remove FABRIC_CAPTURE_LLM_CONTENT; wire capture keeps content off telemetry in the content store

messages.name: spool_migration_ignored
messages.text: spool plaintext migration is ignored in the production profile; plaintext spool records are quarantined
messages.fix: remove FABRIC_WIRE_SPOOL_MIGRATE_PLAINTEXT, or migrate under the local profile first

messages.name: status_file_unwritable
messages.text: the status file could not be written
messages.fix: point FABRIC_WIRE_STATUS_FILE at a writable path in a directory that exists

messages.name: otlp_setting_invalid
messages.text: an OTLP setting is malformed
messages.fix: headers are k=v pairs separated by commas, timeouts are numbers, compression is gzip, deflate or none, and a client key and certificate are set together

messages.name: config_not_found
messages.text: no fabric.yaml was found
messages.fix: create fabric.yaml (schema: fabric.config/v1) in the project directory, or pass --config PATH

messages.name: config_unreadable
messages.text: fabric.yaml could not be read or is not valid YAML
messages.fix: check the file; the message names the line and column

messages.name: config_unknown_key
messages.text: fabric.yaml has a key the schema does not know
messages.fix: remove the key or use the suggested one; the schema is contracts/cli-config/v1/fabric-config-v1.schema.json

messages.name: config_invalid_value
messages.text: a fabric.yaml value is not allowed
messages.fix: use one of the values the message lists

messages.name: cli_extra_missing
messages.text: this command needs the [cli] extra
messages.fix: pip install "singleaxis-fabric[cli]" (or pipx install "singleaxis-fabric[cli]")

messages.name: unknown_command
messages.text: unknown command
messages.fix: run `fabric help` for the list of commands

messages.name: config_schema_unsupported
messages.text: fabric.yaml names a schema this CLI does not support
messages.fix: set schema: fabric.config/v1, or upgrade the CLI

messages.name: provider_url_invalid
messages.text: a provider URL is not a usable model endpoint
messages.fix: give the base URL the client uses, such as https://my-llm.example.com/v1, optionally prefixed anthropic= for the Anthropic dialect

messages.name: env_overrides_config
messages.text: an environment variable overrides a fabric.yaml setting
messages.fix: unset the variable if fabric.yaml should decide

messages.name: command_not_built
messages.text: this command is not part of this release yet
messages.fix: upgrade the CLI; until then follow docs/quickstart.md

messages.name: option_not_built
messages.text: this option is not part of this release yet
messages.fix: use the local profile's defaults; production, Kubernetes and the other destinations follow docs/production-setup.md and docs/deployment.md until the CLI builds them

messages.name: secrets_dir_unsafe
messages.text: the secrets directory is not a private directory of this user
messages.fix: make it a real directory you own with mode 0700 (chmod 700 DIR), or set secrets.dir in fabric.yaml to another path

messages.name: secret_file_unsafe
messages.text: a secret file is a symlink, is not a regular file, or is open to other users
messages.fix: restore it as your own regular file with mode 0600 (chmod 600 FILE), or replace it with `fabric init --rotate NAME`

messages.name: secret_set_incomplete
messages.text: a generated certificate is missing its key or its CA
messages.fix: run `fabric init --rotate ca` to issue a new CA and Node certificate, then `fabric up` and restart agents

messages.name: rotation_needs_restart
messages.text: a rotated secret is still in use by running processes
messages.fix: run `fabric up` so the Node restarts with it; restart agents when the CA or the id key changed

messages.name: config_secret_shaped
messages.text: fabric.yaml must not hold a secret value
messages.fix: put the value in a file and name the file's path (start a relative path with ./); `fabric init` generates and stores secrets itself

messages.name: env_not_imported
messages.text: an environment setting could not be written into fabric.yaml
messages.fix: keep exporting the variable (a variable already set wins over fabric.yaml), or pass --import-secrets to store a key given by value as a file

messages.name: docker_missing
messages.text: Docker with Compose v2 is not installed or not on PATH
messages.fix: install Docker Engine or Docker Desktop (the `docker compose` plugin included), then run the command again

messages.name: docker_not_running
messages.text: the Docker daemon did not answer
messages.fix: start Docker Desktop or the docker service and check `docker info`; on Linux add your user to the docker group or use sudo

messages.name: compose_failed
messages.text: Docker Compose could not apply the Fabric project
messages.fix: read the detail (Docker's own last lines); `docker compose -p fabric-PROJECT logs` shows the services' output

messages.name: port_in_use
messages.text: the Node's port is already in use on this machine
messages.fix: stop the other listener (an earlier local stack: `fabric down` in that project, or `make down` in deploy/compose), or set node.endpoint: https://localhost:PORT in fabric.yaml and run `fabric up` again

messages.name: node_not_healthy
messages.text: the Fabric Node did not answer over TLS in time
messages.fix: run `fabric up --wait 180` to allow a slow first image pull; the detail holds the Node's last log line

messages.name: node_external
messages.text: node.mode is external: there is nothing for this command to start or stop
messages.fix: nothing to do; set node.mode: docker in fabric.yaml to have `fabric up` run a local Node

messages.name: certificate_renewed
messages.text: the Node certificate was close to expiry and was reissued from the local CA
messages.fix: nothing to do: agents trust the CA, which did not change

messages.name: project_changed
messages.text: the running project differed from fabric.yaml or this CLI's pinned images and was updated
messages.fix: nothing to do; the detail names what changed

messages.name: ca_expired
messages.text: the local CA has expired
messages.fix: run `fabric init --rotate ca`, then `fabric up`, then restart agents so they load the new CA

messages.name: image_override
messages.text: an environment variable replaces an image pinned by this CLI release
messages.fix: unset the variable to run the pinned, signed release image; keep it only to test a locally built image

messages.name: state_not_removed
messages.text: part of the project's local state could not be removed
messages.fix: remove the directory named in the detail by hand (files written by a container running as root need sudo)

messages.name: compose_project_not_this_projects
messages.text: the Compose project this command would act on holds containers of another project, so nothing was started, stopped or removed
messages.fix: two projects with the same name share one Compose project: set a different `project:` in this directory's fabric.yaml and run the command again, or run `fabric down` in the directory named in the detail first

messages.name: referenced_secret_unreadable
messages.text: a secret file fabric.yaml references is missing or not a readable regular file, so agents given the compiled environment would capture nothing with it
messages.fix: correct the path in fabric.yaml (secrets.id_key_file or secrets.ca_file) and run `fabric init` again, or remove the setting so `fabric init` generates the secret

messages.name: project_flag_not_the_files
messages.text: --project names another project than the fabric.yaml this command found, so nothing was done
messages.fix: drop --project (fabric.yaml names the project), pass --config with that project's fabric.yaml, or rename this project with `fabric down` and then `fabric init --project NAME`

messages.name: sensor_started
messages.text: the host sensor is running and scoped to this project's agent cgroup
messages.fix: start the agent with `fabric run -- CMD`, which joins this cgroup on Linux; a process started another way is outside the sensor's scope unless its shell joins first (`echo $$ | sudo tee DETAIL/cgroup.procs`)

messages.name: sensor_off
messages.text: the host sensor is off by configuration
messages.fix: set sensor.kind: auto in fabric.yaml and drop --no-sensor to start it where it can load

messages.name: sensor_desktop_vm
messages.text: the host sensor runs inside the Docker VM: it cannot see a process started directly on this machine
messages.fix: nothing to do for capture from the SDK, which is unaffected; for independent host evidence run the agent on a Linux host

messages.name: sensor_kernel_unsupported
messages.text: this kernel cannot load the eBPF sensor (it needs Linux 5.8 or later with BTF and cgroup v2)
messages.fix: use a host with a newer kernel; capture from the SDK is unaffected, only independent host evidence is missing

messages.name: sensor_cgroup_not_permitted
messages.text: the agent cgroup for the host sensor could not be created
messages.fix: run `fabric up` once with sudo, or from a systemd user session (a delegated cgroup); capture from the SDK is unaffected

messages.name: sensor_start_failed
messages.text: the host sensor container did not stay running
messages.fix: read the detail (the sensor's last log line); `fabric up --no-sensor` continues without host evidence

messages.name: sensor_auditd_available
messages.text: eBPF cannot load here but auditd is present on this host
messages.fix: follow docs/host-sensors.md to run the auditd sensor collector; the CLI does not start it in this release

messages.name: sensor_sandboxed_runtime
messages.text: this machine runs inside a sandbox or container that hides the host kernel from the sensor
messages.fix: run `fabric up` on the host itself for host evidence; capture from the SDK is unaffected

messages.name: node_not_started
messages.text: `fabric up` has not started this project's local Node, so the agent's records wait in its spool
messages.fix: run `fabric up`; the spool delivers the records once the Node answers

messages.name: sdk_version_skew
messages.text: the agent's SDK and this CLI are more than one minor version apart
messages.fix: upgrade the older one so both come from the same release (pip install -U "singleaxis-fabric[otlp]" in the agent's environment, or upgrade the CLI)

messages.name: run_sdk_missing
messages.text: the agent's Python interpreter cannot load the Fabric SDK, so this run is not captured; the agent ran unchanged
messages.fix: install the SDK in the agent's own environment with the command in the detail (python -m pip install "singleaxis-fabric[otlp]" with that interpreter), then start the agent again

messages.name: run_otlp_exporter_missing
messages.text: the agent's environment has the Fabric SDK but not the OTLP exporter that sends records to the Node, so this run is not captured; the agent ran unchanged
messages.fix: install the [otlp] extra in the agent's environment with the command in the detail, then start the agent again

messages.name: run_config_unusable
messages.text: the project's configuration could not be used, so the agent ran without capture
messages.fix: run `fabric doctor` in the project directory: it names the problem and its fix (the detail names the first one)

messages.name: run_env_only
messages.text: this command is not a Python program `fabric run` can turn capture on for; it was given the run's Fabric settings only
messages.fix: start a Python agent through its interpreter (fabric run -- python app.py) or the project's .venv; a launcher script can export `fabric run --print-env` itself; Node.js and compiled agents record through the explicit API and the host sensor

messages.name: run_cgroup_join_failed
messages.text: the agent could not join the host sensor's cgroup, so the sensor does not observe this run
messages.fix: start the agent as the user that ran `fabric up`, or run `fabric up` from a systemd user session (a delegated cgroup); capture by the SDK is unaffected

messages.name: run_command_not_found
messages.text: the agent command could not be started
messages.fix: check the command name, that it is on PATH and that it is executable; the detail names it

messages.name: run_no_command
messages.text: `fabric run` needs the agent command after --
messages.fix: fabric run -- python agent.py

messages.name: run_state_unwritable
messages.text: the run could not be recorded under .fabric/state, so it ran without capture and `fabric verify` and `fabric show` do not see it
messages.fix: make the project's .fabric directory a real directory writable by this user (not a symlink), then start the agent again

messages.name: run_capture_off_by_flag
messages.text: capture is off for this run (--no-capture): the agent ran with its environment unchanged
messages.fix: drop --no-capture to record the run

messages.name: run_label_invalid
messages.text: the --run label is not usable, so a generated label was used
messages.fix: use 1-64 letters, digits and ._- for --run

messages.name: compiled_env_stale
messages.text: .fabric/compiled.env is missing or was made from an older fabric.yaml
messages.fix: run `fabric init` (or `fabric up`) to rewrite it; `fabric run` compiles fabric.yaml itself and is not affected, launchers that read the file are

messages.name: node_unreachable
messages.text: the Fabric Node did not answer over TLS with the project's CA
messages.fix: run `fabric up`; if it is running, `fabric doctor` prints its last log line (docker compose -p fabric-PROJECT logs fabric-node shows more)

messages.name: canary_not_captured
messages.text: the canary could not record a model exchange with this project's configuration
messages.fix: the detail holds the SDK's reason and fix; `fabric doctor` checks the same configuration

messages.name: canary_not_delivered
messages.text: the canary's records did not reach the destination in time
messages.fix: check that the Node runs (`fabric up`) and answers (`fabric doctor`); on a slow machine allow more time with fabric verify --wait 120

messages.name: canary_incomplete
messages.text: the canary run was read back but is not complete
messages.fix: each reason in the detail names its fix; python -m fabric.reconstruct --spans DATA/spans --run LABEL prints the full report

messages.name: canary_complete
messages.text: the canary went through capture, the Node and the destination and was read back complete
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: no_run_recorded
messages.text: no `fabric run` is recorded in this project yet, so only the path was checked
messages.fix: start the agent with `fabric run -- CMD`, then run `fabric verify` again

messages.name: run_not_found
messages.text: the run's records were not found in the destination
messages.fix: check the label (`fabric show --list`); a run still in progress or just ended may not be delivered yet: run the command again after the agent exits

messages.name: run_incomplete
messages.text: the run's records are not complete in the reader's verdict
messages.fix: each reason in the detail names its fix; `fabric show` displays what was recorded

messages.name: run_complete
messages.text: the run's records were read back complete and its model decisions were recorded
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: run_not_captured
messages.text: the run was started without capture
messages.fix: the detail lists the reasons recorded when it started; `fabric doctor` shows each with its fix

messages.name: records_unreadable
messages.text: the destination's span files could not be read
messages.fix: the detail names the input and the accepted forms; check the destination directory

messages.name: destination_not_readable
messages.text: this destination is not one Fabric can read back, so records were checked only up to the Node
messages.fix: pass --spans PATH with an export of the destination's spans, or use the local-dir destination

messages.name: no_runs
messages.text: no `fabric run` is recorded in this project
messages.fix: start the agent with `fabric run -- CMD`

messages.name: content_hidden
messages.text: content is not printed because stdout is not a terminal
messages.fix: pass --content to print it

messages.name: manual_setup
messages.text: no fabric.yaml was found: checking this shell's FABRIC_* environment as a manual setup
messages.fix: nothing to do for a manual setup; `fabric init --from-env` writes fabric.yaml from it

messages.name: sdk_ready
messages.text: the agent's Python environment loads the Fabric SDK with this project's settings and reports no problem
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: other_fabric_on_path
messages.text: another program named fabric comes first on PATH
messages.fix: use the singleaxis-fabric command, which is always this CLI, or put this CLI's directory first on PATH

messages.name: sensor_stopped
messages.text: `fabric up` started the host sensor, but its container is not running now
messages.fix: run `fabric up` again; the detail holds the sensor's last log line

messages.name: node_ok
messages.text: the Fabric Node answers over TLS with the project's CA
messages.fix: nothing to do

messages.name: no_status_file
messages.text: the last run left no status file: its agent never loaded the SDK, or was stopped before it started
messages.fix: start the agent with `fabric run` again; if this repeats, the agent's interpreter is not the one with the SDK (`fabric doctor` names the one it checked)

messages.name: no_problem_found
messages.text: no problem found
messages.fix: nothing to do
